title: と共に — “together with ～ / along with ～”
summary: と共に has two main uses. After a person or thing it means “together with ～.” After a change or event it means “along with ～; as ～ happens, … also happens.” It is somewhat formal and common in writing.

patterns.form: 名詞（人） ＋ と共に ＋ 動詞
patterns.gloss: person + と共に: together with (家族と共に)

patterns.form: 名詞（変化） ／ 動詞辞書形 ＋ と共に
patterns.gloss: change noun / dictionary form + と共に: along with, as (発展と共に, 年を取ると共に)

body.p: After a person, と共に means the same as と一緒に but is more formal. 家族と共に、新しい町で暮らし始めた. It can describe a shared action or experience.
After a noun showing change or a verb's dictionary form, it says that two changes happen in step: 経済の発展と共に、生活が便利になった. The first is the trend, and the second changes with it.
The second half can also state a simultaneous event: 卒業と共に、新しい生活が始まった. Compared with ～につれて, と共に includes a stronger sense of “at the same time.”

examples.ja: 経済（けいざい）の発展（はってん）と共（とも）に、生活（せいかつ）が便利（べんり）になった。
examples.romaji: Keizai no hatten to tomo ni, seikatsu ga benri ni natta.
examples.tr: Along with economic development, life became more convenient.

examples.ja: 年（とし）を取（と）ると共（とも）に、記憶力（きおくりょく）が落（お）ちてきた。
examples.romaji: Toshi o toru to tomo ni, kioku-ryoku ga ochite kita.
examples.tr: As I have grown older, my memory has declined.

examples.ja: 家族（かぞく）と共（とも）に、新（あたら）しい町（まち）で暮（く）らし始（はじ）めた。
examples.romaji: Kazoku to tomo ni, atarashii machi de kurashi hajimeta.
examples.tr: I started living in a new town together with my family.

pitfalls: For the “along with a change” meaning, the first part must show a change or an event, not an ordinary noun.
It is formal. In casual talk, use と一緒に.
